projects.name: Pythe
projects.description: An AI cofounder that learns your startup, researches your market and builds a roadmap, then coordinates a team of agents to work through it.
paragraphs: I'm building Pythe with Daiwik because getting an idea built is only part of starting a company. Figuring out what to work on, finding customers and actually growing it is the harder part.

You bring your idea or the company you've already started. We're developing Pythe to learn the context, research competitors and put together a roadmap with daily tasks. Pytheus, the AI cofounder, is designed to delegate work to a team of AI employees instead of leaving you with another list of advice.

We're building the agent system around employees with their own virtual computers, shared startup context and connections to the tools you already use. These features are being developed for launch. I've also made the dynamic product demo videos on the landing page myself.

projects.name: Blertly
projects.description: An AI study app for GCSE and A-Level students, built around active recall, exam practice and feedback you can actually use.
paragraphs: Blertly is one of my first startups, built with friends including my co-founder Dhrishiv. It's an AI revision app for students who want to do more than reread notes and hope they remember them.

The main loop is simple: read a topic, close the notes and blurt out what you remember. The AI checks your answer against the important points, shows you what you missed and helps you work on the gaps.
Alongside blurting, there are revision notes, exam questions with AI marking, handwritten-answer marking and a voice tutor. The aim is to keep learning, practice and feedback in one place.

projects.name: Pico
projects.role: Personal side project; also called Halo
projects.description: An AI desktop agent that can see your screen and use your Windows computer through mouse and keyboard actions.
paragraphs: Pico, also called Halo, is a personal project exploring what it looks like for an AI agent to use a laptop the way a person would.

It takes screenshots, uses a model to work out the next action, then controls the mouse and keyboard through a local Node.js bridge. A floating interface keeps the agent close to the work instead of putting everything in another browser tab.
I built it to experiment with computer use and tested it on computer and operating-system tasks. The project is open source, with a Windows download and the code on GitHub.
projects.result: Public source code and a Windows download.

projects.name: Vistara AI
projects.description: A study-planning project I started to help balance school with everything I wanted to build outside it.
paragraphs: I started Vistara AI because I found it hard to balance school, extracurriculars, sport and the things I enjoyed, like coding and shipping projects.
It was my first study startup, built around a problem I was dealing with myself. It came before Blertly and was an early step from learning to code to building something other people could use.
